validity.recommendation: no action needed; existence, length, diameter, start year and cost all independently corroborated
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed by THREE independent sources naming this exact three-point line (Ain Sokhna / Al-Hafayer / Wadi Hagool): (1) Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum year-end press release (petroleum.gov.eg, 2019-12-30), an official primary source, which states verbatim 'خط خام السخنة /الحفاير/وادى حجول بطول 42 كم وقطر 30 بوصة' (crude line Sokhna/Al-Hafayer/Wadi Hagool, 42 km, 30-inch diameter) -- this is an EXACT match to GEM's Length (42.00 km) AND Diameter (30 in), and is a materially stronger ref than the one currently in the sheet's Diameter [ref] cell (petrojet.com.eg, which is a client-rendered SPA with no server-side content -- url_verifier correctly failed it, and WebFetch/curl confirm the raw HTML carries no project text at all, so it cannot actually be verified as supporting anything; it should not be relied on alone). (2) youm7.com (2021-12-19, major Egyptian daily) names the same three-point corridor ('خط نقل السولار "السخنة/ الحفاير/ وادى حجول"') and gives 41 km -- 1 km off GEM's 42 km, and calls it a DIESEL (سولار) line rather than 'crude' (خام) as the ministry does. (3) egyptoil-gas.com's pipeline-overview feature explicitly states 'Egypt constructed the Ain Sokhna/Wadi hagool/Al-Hafayer pipeline with investments EGP219.2 million in 2018' -- this is an EXACT match to GEM's Cost (219,200,000 EGP) and StartYear1 (2018); the current worklist's automated value_checked flagged this ref as not supporting the cost/year, but that is a substring-matching artifact ('EGP219.2 million' vs the checker's literal '219,200,000' string) -- manually confirmed via url_verifier with tokens '219.2'+'2018' that the page does support both values. CLASSIFICATION: no error -- GEM's generic Fuel value 'Oil, oil products' is broad enough to cover the crude/diesel product-type ambiguity between the two press sources (see caveat below). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster; no other row shares this route, length, or diameter combination. Several other rows terminate at a similarly-named 'El-Hafair' hub (P7975, P7976, P7977, P7978) but with different endpoints, lengths and diameters -- consistent with a real multi-pipeline junction, not a duplicate of P7327. CAVEAT (spec, minor): the two press sources disagree on product type (ministry: crude/خام; youm7: diesel/سولار) and length varies 41 vs 42 km across them -- the sheet's own existing RouteNotes already flags this uncertainty ('IM: ending is unclear, this is a possible route based on satellite imagery but the length doesn't match'), so this is a known, already-documented open question rather than a new defect; the government source's exact match on BOTH length and diameter (42 km / 30 in) is the stronger of the two and should be treated as primary. Status=operating is corroborated contextually by both the 2019 ministry release (listed among completed year-end infrastructure accomplishments) and the 2021 youm7 article (described in the past/present as built infrastructure), though neither uses the literal word 'operating' -- tier medium. The two dead/blocked existing refs (zawya.com HTTP 400, gate.ahram.org.eg HTTP 403) are blocks, not confirmed deletions -- left in place per standing rule, not proposed for removal, but not usable as new verified citations either.

validity.recommendation: no value change recommended (42 km / 30 in stays, backed by the exact-match official government source); optionally note the 41 km / 'diesel-not-crude' variant from youm7 in ResearcherNotes as an unresolved product-type/length nuance -- not material enough to override the primary government figure
validity.researcher_notes: Two independent Egyptian press sources describing what appears to be the same Ain Sokhna-Al-Hafayer-Wadi Hagool corridor disagree on (a) exact length -- 42 km (ministry, matches GEM) vs 41 km (youm7) -- and (b) product carried -- 'crude' (خام, ministry) vs 'diesel' (سولار, youm7). Both are too close in length and identical in named endpoints to plausibly be two separate physical pipelines rather than one line described slightly differently by two writers two years apart; treating this as ONE line (matching GEM's single P7327 row) is the better-supported reading. Diameter (30 in) has only one directly-verified source (the ministry release) since petrojet.com.eg's page cannot be verified (JS-rendered shell, no confirmable text) -- tier medium on diameter alone, tier high on length+existence given the two-source agreement.

summary: P7327 confirmed real (3 independent sources name this exact corridor); no duplicate/classification/existence problems found. Length(42km)+Diameter(30in) get an exact-match upgrade from Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum (petroleum.gov.eg, replacing the unverifiable petrojet.com.eg SPA ref); Cost+StartYear2018 confirmed via egyptoil-gas.com (the worklist's automated check had flagged this ref as non-supporting -- false negative, manually verified as a strong match). One minor open caveat: youm7 names the same corridor as a 41km 'diesel' line vs the ministry's 42km 'crude' line -- treated as one pipeline described two ways, not a duplicate; flagged in researcher_notes, no value change recommended. No UNRESOLVED items; Capacity remains legitimately blank (no source found, not fabricated).
